name: 20th Naval Construction Battalion
note: Seabees. Formed at the Naval Construction Training Center, Norfolk, August 1942. Sailed from Port Hueneme in two waves (6 Oct and 26 Nov 1942) and reunited at Nouméa on 13 Dec 1942. In May-June 1943 it split: a Forward Echelon of about 500 men (the 1st Section) went to Townsville, Woodlark and Kiriwina with the Seventh Fleet; the Rear Echelon (the 2nd Section; its rolls are headed "Detachment" in Sep 1943 and "Second Section" from Dec 1943) went by Guadalcanal and the Russells to New Georgia with the Third Fleet. Reunited on Banika, Russell Islands, 6 Jun 1944; home in September 1944; Okinawa in 1945; broken up there on 29 Aug 1945, its men transferred to the 15th, 36th, 79th and 126th Battalions (ncbhist-020/p2-p3; rg24-190273312/p0835). Its 1942 rolls number the sections the other way round: the roll headed "Sec 2" in Oct 1942 is the first wave, forwarded from Nouméa, while "Section 1" was still at Port Hueneme.

name: 79th Naval Construction Battalion
note: Seabees. Formed at Norfolk; Gulfport and Port Hueneme, then Alaska (Kodiak, Amchitka and Cold Bay), May 1943 - September 1944; Camp Parks; Saipan and Okinawa, 1945, in the 11th Construction Brigade (ncbhist-079/p2-p3). Only its 1945 is transcribed here.
